destination_poi.description_summer:
Säntis is the highest peak of the Alpstein range and a unique viewpoint on the north-eastern end of the Swiss Alps. From here the five neighbouring countries of Switzerland can be seen. The border of the St. Gall and Appenzell cantons meets at the summit. 
The first cabin to house visitors was built in 1846 and since then has been continuously enlarged to become the guesthouse it is today. In 1882 the first meteorological station was installed, while in the second half of the 20th century the radio transmitting installations were added. The aerial cableway from Schwägalp was built between 1933 and 1935. Transporting passengers metres of vertical height in 10 minutes, it is one of the most popular cableways in Switzerland.
destination_poi.description_winter:
Säntis, called the «King of Eastern Switzerland», is not really a mountain to climb by skis. There is an aerial cableway from Schwägalp. The mountain top is full of tourism ballyhoo, but the view is one of the best in the Alps. Of interest are the descents via Wagenlücke to Wasserauen and from the interstation at pillar 2 to Unterwasser, which are often undertaken in good conditions. Both descents have no re-ascents, but they are in steep terrain and require good skiing skills. Säntis is often the starting point for other destinations in the Alpstein range. If the conditions are perfect, its steep slopes and couloirs can be skied down. However, many of these variants are very challenging and are not described (e.g. Chalbersäntis – Schooss or Tierwis – Schwägalp). The Alter Säntis guesthouse (call 071 799 11 60) is sometimes open. If it is, you can spend the night on Säntis. 
Attention: The aerial cableway does not transport any skiers or snowboarders when the danger level for avalanches is "considerable" (3) or above! If in doubt, call 071 365 65 65. Otherwise you might be stuck on Schwägalp.

photos.caption: Öhrli (Öhrlikopf) viewed from Hintere Öhrligrueb at the end of the Nasenlöcher route
The nostrils - the trail to the actual "holes" is a dead end

segments.description: From Schwägalp follow the marked roads up and down to reach Chamm and Potersalp. The bifurcation for the Nasenlöcher route is at ca. 1400 m shortly before Schwizerälpli (signpost).
segments.title: Schwägalp – Potersalp

segments.description: Ascend on the white-blue marked trail overcoming a number of escarpments and past Nasenlöcher. The upper part is a long traverse eastward to reach the picturesque Hintere Öhrligrueb. Turning eastward, you reach the saddle of P. 2117.
segments.title: Potersalp - Hintere Öhrligrueb

segments.description: On the saddle the unmarked, but easy to find ascent to Öhrlikopf begins. At first follow a faint path in the talus to reach the ridge. Overcoming an escarpment, you reach a chimney in the summit structure. Follow the chimney full of scree to the summit ridge. The descent back to Hintere Öhrligrueb is on the ascent route.
segments.title: Detour to Öhrlikopf

segments.description: Follow the white-red mountain hiking trail across the dwindling Blauschnee. The exact itinerary depends on the snow situation and climb up Himmelsleiter (steps cut into the rock) to reach the Säntis summit. Take the aerial cableway down to Schwägalp.
segments.title: Hintere Öhrligrueb – Säntis

segments.description:
Traversing Hüenerberg is an alternative to the crowded Ebenalp-Säntis hiking trail, which is 150 metres of vertical height down on karst. From the Höchnideri saddle hike pathless on karst to the ridge at P. 2246. Now follows a narrow, exposed ridge (T5) with some short climbing passages (grade I and II). P. 2311 and P. 2308 are traversed to reach Hüenerbergsattel (P. 2324), where the Chammhalden route merges from the north. From here descend a few metres southward to reach the mountain hiking trail to Säntis (T4). 
Add ½–1 h for traversing Hüenerberg.

photos.caption: Variant: following the Hüenerberg summit ridge; on the right is Girenspitz, on the left Säntis.

segments.title: Variant: across Hüenerberg

teaser: With the usual and Chammhalden routes this is the third itinerary on the Säntis north face (second in terms of difficulty). Steep, equipped with steel cables and marked white-blue (alpine hiking route), it leads 600 metres of vertical height to Hintere Öhrligrueb. The detour to Öhrlikopf (on the national map new "Öhrlikopf") with some scrambling in shell limestone seems more difficult than it really is. Towards the end of the tour the often crowded mountain hiking route Ebenalp-Schäfler-Säntis can be avoided by undertaking the described, demanding ridge hike.
title: From Schwägalp via Nasenlöcher

reference_poi.description_summer:
Gratabschnitt zwischen Höch Nideri-Sattel und Hüenerbergsattel, der auf der einen Seite einen Teil der hier rund 1000 Meter hohen Nordflanke des Säntismassivs bildet. Die Südseite des Hüenerbergs fällt jedoch lediglich wenige 10 Meter nach Süden auf die Karrenfelder oberhalb der Rossegg ab. Von dieser Seite aus kann der Grat an ziemlich jeder beliebigen Stelle erreicht werden.
Der Hüenerberg, eigentlich der Hüenervogelberg, weist auf den Hüenervogel, den Bussard hin.

Der Hauptkette nordseits vorgelagerter, markanter Felsfirst. Er bietet den einigermassen gewandten Wanderern auf ihrem Weg von Schäfler zum Säntis einen lohnenden Abstecher.
Der Ostgrat wurde etwa 1870 von Johann Jakob Weilenmann, einem Alpenpionier und Gründer des SAC, erstmals begangen.

description.description:
Schwägalp - Potersalp - Nasenlöcher - Hintere Öhrligrueb - Öhrlikopf: 3 h
Öhrlikopf - Hintere Öhrligrueb - Höchnideri saddle P. 2121 - Blauschnee - Säntis: 1½ h
Without the detour to Öhrlikopf ½ h less.

The most exposed passages of the Nasenlöcher route are equipped with steel cables. Some passages require easy climbing (grade I). After rainfall the itinerary remains wet for a rather long time. In this case additional caution is advised. The bonus of the tour, Öhrlikopf, is climbed through chimneys (grade I). The loose rubble on the faces requires attention when several climbers are on the way to the summit.
